seed: New Layer via Cut, Shift Command J. A marquee round the heading of a screenshot, one key, and the heading lifts onto a layer of its own while the page it was sitting on fills back in with the colour that was around it. The proof is the drag afterwards: pull the new layer clear and what it came off is clean page, not a hole and not a second copy of the same words. The second half of the walk presses the same key over a marquee on a rectangle, where there is no bitmap for the space to go in, so it must refuse out loud rather than go quiet.

steps.note: a screenshot dropped and picked. Its top left corner sits at 720,400, so the General heading is at 731,411 to 772,424 in window points
a marquee snug round the word General, which is sitting on flat page colour on every side

THE TEST: one press makes a third layer, the piece, and it is the one picked. The marquee is gone, it has done its job. copied must read 'none': the surroundings were one flat colour, so the fill was READ and nothing needed saying
THE TEST: the new layer pulled right off the screenshot. Where the heading was is clean page, not a hole and not a second copy of the word
THE TEST: one undo takes back the drag and ONE more takes back the whole cut, the piece and the hole and the fill together. Back to two layers and the screenshot whole
a marquee over the left half of a rectangle, rectangle still picked. There is no bitmap for the space to go in

THE TEST: the key must not go quiet. Layers stays 3, and copied reads 'Cannot cut a piece onto its own layer - Only a picture can have a piece taken out. Turn it into a picture from the Layer menu, then try again.' NOT 'clear the marquee to cut the whole layer', because clearing it makes Command J duplicate the layer and cut nothing
